done_when: The commit hook refuses only when git commit itself is given -n or --no-verify, never for an -n that belongs to another command on the same line

findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

Raise: Not done. For `git commit -F - <<EOF` with a message line `\$(git commit -n)` before `EOF`, the backslash makes the substitution literal, so the invoked commit has no prohibited option and no second commit runs. Line 229 nevertheless retains that message line because it contains `$(`. The command scanner then parses `git commit -n` from the message and refuses the harmless commit. The named unquoted-heredoc test covers an executable substitution, but not this literal one.
findings.title: Not done: The commit hook refuses only when git commit itself is given -n or --no-verify, never for an -n that belongs to another command on

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Raise: Security. In an unquoted `git commit -F - <<EOF` heredoc, Bash joins a line ending `E\` with the next line `OF` before checking the delimiter. A following `git commit -n -m x` therefore runs as a shell command. At line 227, the scanner checks the original lines separately, continues discarding text until a later literal `EOF`, and lets the skipped-hooks commit through. The [Bash manual](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.pdf) confirms that backslash-newline joining precedes delimiter matching.
findings.title: Heredoc line continuation hides a skipped-hooks commit

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Raise: Not done. Lines 220–221 recognize stdin commit messages with `-F -`, `--file -`, or `--file=-`, but miss the valid attached form `-F-`. For `git commit -F- <<'EOF'` with a message mentioning `git commit -n`, the scanner retains the message and refuses the commit although it has no skip flag. Line 229 also retains an escaped literal `\$(git commit -n)` in an unquoted stdin message and refuses it as though the substitution ran. The allowed tests cover neither message form. [Git documents `-F` with `-` as stdin](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit).

why: The commit hook treats pytest -n 2 on the same command line as git commit as skipping the hooks and refuses the commit
